budgets.name: graph-first-500
budgets.what: Open a repository and lay out the first 500 rows of its graph, from every branch and tag, with the commits on them

budgets.name: graph-first-500
budgets.what: The same, on a repository without a commit-graph file
budgets.note: Not promised. Without generation numbers the exact order needs the whole history walked first, and git itself takes as long. The window closes this: it has git write the commit-graph when a repository lacks one.

budgets.name: window-on-screen
budgets.what: Start the desktop app to its window on the screen, in the theme's colours, before anything is read

budgets.name: window-first-repository
budgets.what: Start the desktop app with a repository open, to the first frame that shows it: its tab in the title bar, its branches in the left column and the first rows of its graph
budgets.note: Not promised. Most of it is the system's webview starting, which the window cannot hurry: some 400 ms on the machine the numbers come from, where a page that draws nothing at all paints no sooner. The window is on the screen long before it, and the repository is read while the webview starts.

budgets.name: window-memory
budgets.what: Three repositories open in the window, each one read and its whole graph laid out: the memory the app and its webview hold together
budgets.note: Not promised on Linux, where it is measured on a CI machine with no GPU: WebKitGTK draws in software on a virtual display, and that costs most of the number before the window shows anything - some 300 MB with nothing but the left column on the screen. The promise is held where the webview draws as it does on a desktop, and every platform's number is published.

budgets.name: window-diff-5000-lines
budgets.what: Open the first diff in the window - the 5 000-line file the core's budget reads, one line in four rewritten - from asking for it to the frame that shows it side by side and highlighted
budgets.note: Not promised yet: measured from its first release on.

budgets.name: status-after-save
budgets.what: Working tree status after a file is saved, in a repository of up to 10 000 files

budgets.name: diff-5000-lines
budgets.what: Open the change of a 5 000-line file that a commit rewrote one line in four: what the commit changed, both sides of the file, and the hunks between them
